findings.summary: The blanket skip of root-cause requests is a special case the existing plain-prose filter already covers. It is only needed because the plan also scans the summary, and it exempts real subjective outcomes in root-cause jobs.
findings.evidence: terms.rs:189-207: `plain_request_prose` already drops the 'Fix the root cause of a repeated failure:', 'Failure class:', 'Cause:' and 'Introspection ... prevention it proposed:' lines when ROOT_CAUSE_ANCHOR is present (is_generated_line, terms.rs:62-80). With those lines dropped, this job's request has no trigger. Only the accepted reading's summary ('such as a page being clear to a newcomer') would trigger, and the plan adds the summary scan itself. The plan's own risk list admits that the skip lets a root-cause job that delivers a subjective page through. Fix: Scan only `plain_request_prose(request)` and drop both the summary scan and the whole-request anchor skip. Keep the corpus case subjective-cited-in-root-cause-request, built with generated_root_cause_request, as an Accept case. Add a Refuse case: a root-cause request whose own acceptance bullet asks for a page clear to a newcomer with no method.
findings.location: Decision 3 / Step 2 (skip on ROOT_CAUSE_ANCHOR; scan the reading summary)

findings.summary: A content criterion, or a loosely worded one, satisfies the gate without any check that runs, so the unverifiable-outcome class can recur.
findings.evidence: outcome.rs:304-307: `check_outcome_state` accepts only a Behavior criterion: 'a content criterion that mentions a state still checks only a file, so it does not pass'. The plan accepts any kind. Its persona matcher ('as a ', 'as an ') and threshold matcher ('below' or 'blocks' plus any digit) match incidental wording, so a content criterion such as 'docs/x.md, as a reference, says an independent reviewer rates it 1-5 and blocks below 3' passes. Fix: Require `CriterionKind::Behavior` for the method criterion, as check_outcome_state does. Tighten persona to a named persona word or 'reads it as a/an <noun>'. Require the threshold digit to sit next to the threshold word. Add a Refuse unit case where the full method appears only in a content criterion.
findings.location: Decision 4 (satisfied by one criterion of any kind; persona matches 'as a ', 'as an ')

findings.summary: The dependents list omits the athena-cli readers of `check_reading_text`.
findings.evidence: crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs:4049-4095 calls `check_reading_text` on UNREAD_FIRST/UNREAD_SECOND and asserts Refuse/Accept. crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs:102 documents that drain relies on the text-only checks. The plan lists only main.rs:652, replay.rs, run/tests.rs and steward.rs. (I read the fixtures: 'demo study ... intro' holds no trigger, so the test should still pass, but the list must name it.) Fix: Add crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs (the test around line 4049) and crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs to the dependents, with the test `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain`, and state that the fixtures hold no trigger phrase.

findings.summary: The new artifact-noun list duplicates the existing `VISIBLE_NOUNS`.
findings.evidence: outcome.rs:48-49 defines `pub(super) const VISIBLE_NOUNS: [&str; 13]`, documented as 'Things an audience sees' (page, pages, site, website, ...), which `check_outcome_state` already uses. Fix: Reuse `VISIBLE_NOUNS`, extending it there if a noun such as explainer or tutorial is missing, so the two checks cannot drift.

findings.summary: 'readable', 'site' and 'manual' have common technical senses, so the trigger can refuse ordinary code requests (criterion 6).
findings.evidence: has_phrase (surveys.rs:39-45) treats a hyphen as a word boundary, so 'machine-readable' and 'human-readable' match 'readable'. 'call site' and 'manual step' contain artifact nouns. Athena's own steward writes 'Make the {source} source readable to the steward' (steward.rs:771), using 'readable' in the access sense. Fix: Drop bare 'readable' or require it not to follow a hyphen, and drop 'site' after 'call' and 'manual' as an adjective (or drop 'manual'). Add Accept corpus cases such as 'Make each call site readable' and 'Make the page output machine-readable'.

findings.summary: `git diff --stat` cannot run in the verifier's plain copy, which has no git, and listing files is existence evidence.
findings.evidence: System facts: the reader, planner and critic get a plain copy without git. The criterion is [content], so this does not block. Fix: Phrase the check as reading the candidate diff's file list, and keep the 'before the build' assertion as the behavioral part.

summary: The plan puts the fix in the right place: one new `step!` line at the end of `refusing_check` (checks.rs:529-543). The names it relies on all exist: `has_phrase` (surveys.rs:39), `plain_request_prose`/`plain_line`/`ROOT_CAUSE_ANCHOR` (terms.rs:52,177,189), `refuser_for`/`terms_reading`/`reading_source` (reading.rs:6609,6614,1368), INPUT_FORMS of 41, `generated_root_cause_request`, `environment_reach_refusal_is_declared_intended`, `replay_declaration` in refusal_corpus.rs, and the READING_RULES test with its 9-rule count and 2750-byte bound (briefs.rs:4530-4581). The demonstrations run the production gate and would fail without the step. Three things need revising. (1) The plan skips any request that holds the root-cause anchor. That special case is only needed because the plan also scans the reading summary. `plain_request_prose` already drops the generated lines that quote the cause, so scanning only the request removes the need for the skip and closes the hole the skip opens. (2) A criterion of any kind satisfies the method, and the persona test ("as a ") matches almost any sentence. A content criterion that names a reader and a 1 to 5 rating still only checks a file, so the class can recur. The sibling `check_outcome_state` requires a Behavior criterion for exactly this reason. (3) The dependents list leaves out the cli drain test that calls `check_reading_text`. Minor: the plan duplicates outcome.rs's `VISIBLE_NOUNS`, and the trigger nouns "site" and "manual" plus the word "readable" have common technical senses.
